content:
The image shows a corn ear with extensive dark blue-green to gray-green mold covering the kernels from the base through most of the ear. The kernels beneath are orange/yellow but largely obscured by the fungal growth between and on them.

Key features observed:
- Dark blue-green/gray-green conidia coating the kernel surfaces
- Mold distributed across all kernels, not just the tip
- Coverage appears to span from the base/middle outward, covering essentially the whole visible ear
- Color is dark green, not olive-green (ruling out Aspergillus) and not confined to the tip (ruling out Penicillium)

This pattern — dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels, covering all kernels from base to middle — matches Trichoderma_Ear_Rot precisely. The symptom description states "massive production of green to gray-green conidia, often covering the entire ear" and "symptoms typically occurring from base to middle of cob covering all kernels and husk leaf layers." The coloration and distribution are characteristic.
